A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAFT study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison; relocated appendix material can be matched without material reading gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on emergent misalignment and spurious-correlation tasks, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and automated interpretation.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and reports additional test-time intervention comparisons and MMLU/GSM8K evaluations, alongside revised automated-interpretation results.

M1.justification: The projection-based CAFT training procedure and PCA/SAE direction discovery remain unchanged. The optional automated direction-selection pipeline changes from GPT-4.1 mini to GPT-4.1 and replaces task-example-based relevance scoring with a target-concept rubric (v1 Appendix H; v2 Appendix C).

E1.justification: V2 adds MMLU and GSM8K as auxiliary evaluations of retained knowledge and mathematical reasoning (Appendix A.6). The three central CAFT task families, including their additional evaluation questions and skyline datasets, are retained.

E2.justification: V2 Appendix A.4 adds inference-only PCA and SAE ablation comparators to the emergent-misalignment experiments. These comparators already appeared for multiple-choice tasks in v1 Appendix F. Existing random/top-direction, checkpoint, secure-training, and skyline comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The automated-interpretation experiment changes its explainer model and relevance-scoring prompt; v2 also documents three few-shot examples. Appendix A.4 introduces inference-only intervention conditions. Existing fine-tuning budgets, dataset sizes, evaluation judges, and scoring thresholds are retained.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends validation by testing whether inference-only interventions suffice and whether CAFT harms general capabilities (A.4 and A.6). It also revises the automated-versus-human interpretation analysis. Earlier threshold sensitivity, SAE variants, multiple-choice ablations, and skylines are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed comparisons, the stated single-seed exceptions, standard errors by default, min–max ranges for Pareto plots, and standard deviations for skyline results. Updated error-bar values and additional results do not establish a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds capability-retention scores and emergent-misalignment inference-only results, and materially revises automated-interpretation outcomes under the changed setup. Section 4.2 revises Qwen's CAFT-PCA misalignment rate from 0.39% to 0.51%; random-PC results also change in Figure 5. Tables that merely reproduce existing plots are not separate experimental additions.

T1.justification: The train/OOD formulation, projection-subspace construction, and attribution approximation are substantively unchanged. V2 clarifies the already-used allowance for generic pretraining/chat data. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: steering generalization through interpreted training-time ablations without modifying training data, demonstrated on three tasks with roughly tenfold reduced misalignment. Added validation does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains inference-time misalignment suppression versus learning an intended algorithm, interprets the new capability checks, and presents automated interpretation more positively while calling it an unoptimized proof of concept. It removes the quantified 2.8-million-token human-interpretation burden; other principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 revises the automated-interpretation prompt and model documentation. It removes explicit access links for two SAE releases and three generated-chat datasets previously given in v1 Appendices I/J. The main code link, training hyperparameters, hardware information, and direction-discovery details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds Kassem et al.'s sparse model diffing work as reference 29 and briefly connects dictionary learning to interpreting fine-tuning changes. The other cited works and the paper's overall research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The appendices are extensively reorganized from A–J into a results-first A–H structure, consolidating skyline and latent-ablation sections. The automated-interpretation discussion is rewritten and its word-count subsection removed. Main-text edits are comparatively limited.

P2.justification: V2 adds five result tables, several tabulating previously plotted evidence, and a new inference-only comparison figure. It redraws several plots and extensively relocates appendix displays. New Figure 12's caption reverses the model panels relative to their plotted baseline results.

improvement.justification: The inference-only controls and capability-retention checks address useful validation gaps, while numerical tables make results easier to inspect. These provide a limited net improvement. Gains are tempered by removed resource-access links and new display inconsistencies: Figure 12 reverses model labels, and Table 7 reports PCA-autointerp gender accuracy of 0.11 whereas Figure 21 plots approximately 0.40.
